title: Energy partitioning of wave packets in one-dimensional systems
authors: Flavia B. Ramos, Imke Schneider, Sebastian Eggert, Rodrigo G. Pereira
abstract: We investigate the non-equilibrium dynamics of wave packets in a one-dimensional critical fermionic system and analyze the resulting partitioning of energy between emergent excitations. Starting from a Gaussian wave packet injected on top of the many-body ground state, we follow its real-time evolution using the time-dependent density-matrix renormalization group. We observe that interactions lead to fractionalization of the initial excitation into counter-propagating left- and right-moving modes, whose energies can be resolved in real space. To interpret these results, we employ Luttinger liquid theory, which allows us to derive analytical predictions for the energy carried by the emergent modes. We find good agreement between field-theoretical predictions and numerical simulations in the low-energy regime. In contrast to charge fractionalization, which is completely determined by the Luttinger liquid parameter, we show that energy partitioning is non-universal and depends on details of the injected wave packet, such as its width. Our results provide a real-space characterization of energy partitioning in one-dimensional systems and establish a quantitative comparison between non-equilibrium numerical simulations and the effective field-theory description.
summary: This work analyzes how injected energy in 1D fermionic systems partitions into left- and right-moving excitations using both tDMRG simulations and Luttinger liquid theory. The key finding is that while charge fractionalization is universal, the energy partitioning is non-universal, depending on the initial wave packet's details. This establishes a quantitative link between real-space dynamics and effective field theory descriptions.
main_problem: The paper investigates the non-equilibrium dynamics and the resulting energy partitioning of wave packets injected into one-dimensional critical fermionic systems.
main_result: Energy partitioning is found to be non-universal, depending on the details of the injected wave packet, contrasting with charge fractionalization which is governed by the Luttinger liquid parameter.
method: The study combines real-time numerical simulations using the time-dependent density-matrix renormalization group (tDMRG) with analytical predictions derived from Luttinger liquid theory (bosonization).
model_or_system: The system is a spinless fermionic model on a 1D lattice with nearest-neighbor interactions, mapping to the XXZ chain in the critical regime. The analysis focuses on the non-equilibrium evolution following the injection of a Gaussian wave packet.
key_observables: Local energy excess ($E_j(t)$), separated left-moving ($\Delta E_L(t)$) and right-moving ($\Delta E_R(t)$) energy components, and fractional charges ($Q_{L,R}$).
important_parameters: Interaction strength ($V$), wave packet width ($\sigma$), momentum ($k_0$), and the Luttinger liquid parameter ($K$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on separating the wave packet into distinct left and right segments, and the field-theoretical approach assumes a continuum limit and specific approximations for correlation functions.
figures_summary: Figures show snapshots of local energy excess separating into left/right components, and plots comparing extracted energy plateaus ($\Delta E(t)$) for varying interaction strengths and wave-packet widths.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the non-equilibrium setup and Hamiltonian, to performing numerical simulations (tDMRG) to observe energy separation, and finally developing and applying Luttinger liquid theory to derive analytical, quantitative predictions for the energy partitioning.
why_interesting: The comparison between non-equilibrium numerical dynamics and established field-theoretical methods (LL theory) provides a rigorous testbed for understanding energy flow and excitation dynamics in strongly correlated 1D systems, which is highly relevant to quantum materials.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Snapshots of the energy excess for V = 0.5, k0 = 0.55π and the times indicated in the figure. The dashed lines indicate the light cone associated to the propagation of the low-energy modes, defined by the velocity v ≈1.299 calculated from Eq. (15). For t = 75, we show energy profiles for σ = 14.5, 10, 7.1, and 5. The inset is a zoom-in of the left-moving hump at t = 75.

Figure 2: (a) Snapshots of the wave-packet dynamics for k0 = 0.6π, σ = 10 and several values of V. The shaded area indicates the left segment used to estimate EL. Panels (b) and (c) respectively show the energies contained in the chain segments j ∈[1, jmax] and j ∈[jmax +1, L −1], with jmax = 125. The color coding for different values of V in these panels correspond follows that in panel (a). The dashed lines indicate the time at which the estimates of EL and ER are extracted.

Figure 3 shows pL as a function of the interaction strength V for several values of k0 and σ. Interestingly, the results clearly show that pL decreases with increasing k0. This behavior highlights the nontrivial momentum dependence of the excitation energy. In addition, for fixed values of k0, our DMRG results show that pL increases as the wave-packet width decreases; see the inset of Fig. 3.

Figure 3: Fraction of the total energy propagating to the left as a function of the interaction strength V for several values of k0 and σ. The solid, dashed, and dotted lines correspond to σ = 14.5, 10, and 8.3, respectively, with each color set denoting a fixed value of k0. The dash-dotted line shows the prediction for local injection from Refs. [22,23]; see Eq. (11). The inset shows the results for k0 = 0.6π and different values of σ in the intermediate- to strong-interaction regime.

Figure 4: QL and pL as a function of k0 obtained for V = 0.5 and σ = 10 . The symbols represent the DMRG estimates. The blue and green dashed lines are the LL predictions for pL and QL, respectively; see Eqs. (8) and (11).
